We have expressed our administration's readiness to partner China Harbour Engineering Company Limited (CHEC) on the comprehensive development of the proposed Abia Sea Port City, from feasibility studies through construction to final delivery.

I made this known yesterday while receiving a delegation led by the company’s Managing Director, Mr. Wang Jason, who presented its preliminary findings and proposals on the project. 

My preference is for a partnership that extends beyond consultancy and feasibility studies to the actual construction and delivery of the project. I emphasised that the State requires honest, professional advice to determine the project’s viability and the most suitable technical direction.

I also emphasised that the proposed arrangement would be a genuine public-private partnership (PPP), assuring the company of our commitment to transparency, integrity and mutually beneficial business relationships. I stressed that our administration does not engage in dishonest practices. I noted that other prospective investors, including Afreximbank, had also expressed interest, with further decisions to be guided by the outcome of the feasibility study.

Mr. Wang Jason described the proposed project as a viable integrated infrastructure development master plan, explaining that the feasibility study would establish the most suitable port design, technical specifications and depth requirements. He also expressed CHEC’s interest in a long-term partnership with Abia State, beyond consultancy services, and commended Aba’s economic significance and potential to support the development.

I am optimistic that, with proper planning, technical expertise, patience and sustained commitment, the proposed port, integrated with other infrastructure and economic activities, can significantly transform Abia’s economic landscape.

Our development vision is anchored on long-term planning and continuity, as reflected in the 25-year development plan already enacted into law to sustain progress beyond successive administrations.

SCOOP: Internal, unreleased AI models at OpenAI and Anthropic are becoming so powerful that many employees believe they can no longer be safely released, according to more than two dozen sources familiar with the internal debates.

This could significantly slow the AI boom, as the gap between what the most advanced AI systems can do and humans' ability to control them continues to widen.

Recent advances have sparked debate at the highest levels of both companies and within the broader AI research community about whether to stop releasing frontier models publicly altogether, instead reserving them for internal use. Some believe the companies should stop training new models entirely.

But even keeping the most powerful models behind closed doors presents risks. Models are becoming better at deceiving the systems designed to monitor them, just as AI companies increasingly rely on AI itself to monitor and develop other AI systems.
Researchers and employees with direct knowledge of the risks of releasing these models told Axios they fear executives will prioritize profits over safety. Multiple employees said they believe executives have become out of touch with the severity of those risks.

The Time is NOW. Congress Must Act.

Almost every day, there is a new story about how AI will transform our world, disrupt our economy or escape human control.

Just yesterday, Alexandr Wang, Meta’s Chief AI Officer, wrote: “It is hard to imagine a world where humanity maintains control with superintelligence that is 1000x smarter and more capable than humans in every field.”

Got it? The Chief AI Officer at Meta is telling us that human beings are on their way to losing control over planet Earth.

He is not alone.

This month, Paul Christiano, an OpenAI Foundation Board member, said it is a coin flip that the current path would lead to an irreversible loss of human control within three years.

In September, Jacob Coxon resigned from Anthropic stating that AI companies are “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.”

Nobel Prize winner Dr. Geoffrey Hinton, the Godfather of AI, says that AI poses a 10% to 20% chance of wiping out humanity.

Nobody has all the answers to this extraordinary crisis, but one thing is clear. The leaders of major AI companies, scientists and experts all agree: humans are losing control of AI technology, with potentially catastrophic results.

So, what has Congress done to regulate AI? Virtually nothing.

That has got to change. Congress must understand the urgency of the moment. 

We need an immediate PAUSE on advanced AI development and a permanent BAN on superintelligence — an artificial mind smarter than any human, capable of operating independently beyond our control. Let us start with the simple idea that AI should not be allowed to build smarter AI by banning “recursive self-improvement.”

The future of humanity cannot be left in the hands of Big Tech oligarchs who are motivated by more wealth and power.

Congress must act NOW before it is too late.
